Configure API Connection
Enter your OpenRouter API key to enable the Synapse AI chatbot and clinical impression generation. Get your key at openrouter.ai. Your key is stored locally on this device only.
📝 Paste Patient Notes
Paste anything you've written down for this patient — clerking notes, referral text, vitals, labs, imaging reports. When you press Continue, AI extracts the details and fills the matching fields in the Patient Information form. Only empty fields are filled — nothing you've already typed is overwritten.
📎 Fill Patient Information from image(s)?
You've attached image(s). AI can read them now and fill in matching empty fields in the Patient Information form, the same way Paste Patient Notes does. Only empty fields are filled — nothing you've already typed is overwritten. You can always do this later when you click Generate Entry or Synapse instead.
Clear Patient Data
This will erase all information entered in the Patient Information tab. This cannot be undone.

Resuscitation & Procedures
ET tube & catheter sizing, adrenaline, exchange transfusion, CPR metronome
ET Tube Sizing & Umbilical Catheter Depth
Weight (g)
ETT length at lips = 6.632 + 1.822×ln(weight in kg). ETT length at nares (mm) = 45 + 1.15×√(birth weight in g). UAC: <1.5kg = wt×4+7; ≥1.5kg = wt×2.5+9.7. UVC = wt×1.5+5.5. All depths in cm unless stated — confirm final position on X-ray.
Adrenaline (Epinephrine) for Neonatal Resuscitation
Weight (kg)
Dose is of 1:10,000 (0.1 mg/mL) adrenaline. IV/IO preferred: 0.01–0.03 mg/kg. ETT (only if no IV/IO access yet): 0.05–0.1 mg/kg. May repeat every 3–5 min per NRP.
Partial Exchange Transfusion (Polycythaemia)
Birth Weight (g)
Current Venous Hct (%)
Small for Gestational Age? (1500–3000g only)
Volume to exchange = Blood Volume × (Observed Hct − Desired Hct) ÷ Observed Hct. Typically exchanged with normal saline via umbilical vessel, in aliquots.
CPR Metronome (NRP 3:1 ratio)
Ready
90 compressions + 30 breaths/min

⚠️ Warning Signs (WHO 2009)
Abdominal pain / tenderness
Persistent vomiting (≥3 episodes/day)
Clinical fluid accumulation (ascites / pleural effusion)
Mucosal bleed (gum, epistaxis, haematuria, vaginal)
Lethargy / restlessness / altered consciousness
Liver enlargement > 2 cm
Rising HCT with rapid platelet fall
🔴 Severe Dengue Features (any = Group C)
Dengue shock — SBP <90 mmHg or pulse pressure <20 mmHg
Severe bleeding (haematemesis, melaena, large haematoma)
Severe organ impairment (liver, CNS, heart, kidneys)
